NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 11 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 22 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 20, 8:48 AM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 11 DraftKings main slate at 22.3 DraftKings points for $7,700, against Miami. Dak Prescott (22.1, $6,700) and Caleb Williams (21.5, $6,300) are next.

Joe Milton III returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.63 projected points per $1,000 at $4,700.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 20, 8:48 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 11

Josh Allen, BUF vs MIA ($7,700)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.3 DraftKings points at $7,700, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 0.2 points clear of Dak Prescott. The model includes 6.6 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.89 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.4 points with a simulated floor of 8.5 and a ceiling of 41.2, and he holds 10% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 16.5-point favorite at home against Miami, with an implied team total of 30.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.

Dak Prescott, DAL vs TEN ($6,700)

Dak Prescott projects 2nd at the position with 22.1 DraftKings points at $6,700, 4th on the main slate overall. The salary works out to 3.30 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Prescott averaged 22.1 points with a simulated floor of 8.5 and a ceiling of 40.5, and he holds 21% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite at home against Tennessee, with an implied team total of 31.5 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Value: Joe Milton III, PHI vs PIT ($4,700)

Joe Milton III projects for 17.1 DraftKings points at $4,700, which works out to 3.63 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 13 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 9.5 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Milton averaged 17.0 points with a simulated floor of 7.0 and a ceiling of 31.1, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Philadelphia is a 3.5-point underdog at home against Pittsburgh, with an implied team total of 17.5 in a game totaled at 38.5.
